Description: The genome-editing technology or technique used to introduce the genetic modification(s) made at this step. If multiple modifications, list in the same order as geneticModificationType.
Valid Values: CRISPR, TALEN, ZFN, RNA interference, base editing, prime editing

Description: Post-transcriptional gene silencing in which double-stranded RNA (e.g. shRNA or siRNA) triggers sequence-specific degradation of the target mRNA. Use for knock-downs.

A technique for the direct conversion of a specific DNA base into another at a targeted genomic locus, using a Cas nickase, or Cas fused to a deaminase, and a guide RNA, without a double-strand break. Use instead of CRISPR when a base editor was used.

A technique for precise genome editing that relies on an RNA-guided Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA) that both specifies the target site and encodes the desired edit. Use instead of CRISPR when a prime editor was used.
